result.topic_en: Concluding remark: for a uniform elastic lamina (S = A) the shear force and tension are expressed through derivatives of y, and eliminating T gives a fourth-order differential equation, as found by earlier authors.
result.transcription:
CORP. SIVE FLEXIBIL. SEV ELASTIC. 413
quae si lamina elastica fuerit aequabilis, ideoque $S = A$,
dabunt statim $V = -A\left(\frac{d^3y}{ds^3}\right)$, hincque $\left(\frac{dT}{ds}\right) = -A\left(\frac{ddy}{ds^2}\right)\left(\frac{d^3y}{ds^3}\right)$,
quae per $ds$ multiplicata et integrata dat $T = B - \frac{A}{2}\left(\frac{ddy}{ds^2}\right)^2$;
vnde eliminando T ad aequationem peruenitur differentia-
lem quarti gradus, quemadmodum etiam inuenerunt ii,
qui hoc argumentum fusius tractauerunt.

DE

items.quote: vnde eliminando T ad aequationem peruenitur differentialem quarti gradus, quemadmodum etiam inuenerunt ii, qui hoc argumentum fusius tractauerunt.
items.english: whence, by eliminating T, one arrives at a differential equation of the fourth degree, just as those who have treated this subject more fully have also found.
